goal: Collect evidence-grounded comparative dossiers for eight adjacent agent-orchestration repositories against Cyberalchemy. This first pipeline stage supplies frozen primary-source evidence to a separately governed synthesis stage.
context: The governing questions and claim discipline are defined in research/agent-orchestration-project-comparison/research-initial-definitions.md. Research must distinguish documentation assertions, implementation witnesses, tests, and executed behavior; absence claims remain bounded to inspected surfaces. Explorer returns will be frozen by the parent before any synthesis dispatch is compiled, preventing unmanifested runtime handoffs.

agents.initial_prompt: Read research/agent-orchestration-project-comparison/research-initial-definitions.md in full. Deeply inspect builderz-labs/mission-control and boundflow/boundflow at a pinned commit or release, recording repository URL, SHA, inspection date, license, and bounded activity indicators. Use primary GitHub evidence: documentation, source, configuration, tests, releases, issues or discussions only when needed. For every load-bearing claim, label evidence as documentation assertion, implementation witness, test witness, or executed observation and provide a stable permalink or exact path plus SHA; README text alone is not implementation proof. Answer RQ2-RQ4 for each repository and contribute evidence to RQ5-RQ13 by comparing against Cyberalchemy's local research definitions and cited project surfaces. Return: repository fact sheets; architecture and workflow reconstruction; capability/evidence matrix; what each has that Cyberalchemy does not propose; what Cyberalchemy has that each lacks on inspected surfaces; reusable mechanisms with concrete source witnesses, dependencies, license constraints, fit risks, and adopt/adapt/reject/investigate candidates; contrary evidence, unresolved questions, and bounded negative claims. Do not modify project artifacts; return a source-ready report to the synthesis stage. Do not recommend implementation or claim novelty.
